17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans — 1720-26 North Clybourn Avenue, Chicago, IL

Proposed Zoning: B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District
Lot Area: Approximately 7,200 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to redevelop the subject property with a new
five-story residential building containing twenty-four (24) dwelling units.
The proposed building will measure 55 ft. in height and will be supported.
by five (5) off-street parking spaces at the rear. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-
0303-D optional Administrative Adjustment and Variation and pursuant to
Secs. 17-13-1101-D and 17-13-1101-B of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance,
the Applicant is seeking to reduce the off-street parking space requirement
from twelve (12) parking spaces to five (5) parking spaces, reduce the rear
setback for the residential units from the required 30 ft. to 18 ft.-4 in., and
is seeking all zoning relief, as needed and as allowed by the Chicago Zoning
Code, for the attached plans.

(A) _ The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 28,800 square feet (3.89 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 300 square feet per D.U.
(24 residential units)

(C) The amount of off-street parking: 5 parking spaces

*Pursuant to Sec, 17-13-1101-D, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the number of

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 491 linear feet of the Ashland and North CTA
bus line corridors (routes 9 and 72, respectively) and within 870 ft. of the Clybourn/North
CTA Red Line Rail station. The proposed residential building containing twenty-four (24)
residential units will be supported by five (5) off-street parking spaces. Pursuant to Section
17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the residential off-street parking ratio
from 50% (12 parking spaces) to 20.08% (5 parking spaces).

2. The Applicant’s building design complies with the main building door and entryway design
standards provided by Sec. 17-4-0504 because the main residential entrance of the
proposed building fronts along Noth Clybourn Avenue and the proposed front setback is
zero. Furthermore, the entrance widths do not exceed 12 ft., the entrance depths do not
exceed the entrance width, the entrances are not more than two-stories in height, and the
proposed building elevations comply with the window transparency requirements.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
residential building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the Clybourn/North CTA red Line Rail Station, the Ashland CTA bus line
corridor, and the North CTA bus line corridor. The Applicant believes the development
will improve the subject area for residents and other commuters traveling in the subject
area.

4, The proposed residential building will contain twenty-four (24) residential units. The
proposed building will be supported by five (5) off-street parking spaces and twelve (12)
onsite bicycle parking spaces. The Applicant is seeking administrative approval to permit
the off-street parking ratio reduction (5 parking spaces proposed) for the residential units
pursuant to the TOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed residential building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace a two-story mixed-
use building and a three-story residential building with a new five-story residential building
along North Clybourn Avenue. The proposed residential units will provide additional
residential housing inventory to meet market demand. Based on the subject property’s
proximity to mass transit, the Applicant believes the project provides transit options and
otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules
promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an area in need.
